title: Have your agent reuse a teammate's task board in a new tool
summary: A developer building a code review tool had an agent find and plug in a colleague's existing task board; the team says it ran within five minutes.
agent_role: The agent found the team's existing task board, added it to the new project and wired it up. The developer set the goal and kept extending the tool.
outcome: The team reports the tool went from first prompt to running in under five minutes, with no changes to the board's code.
what_they_did: A developer on the poster's team was building a tool for reviewing code changes with an agent. He wanted questions about specific lines to become tickets that agents pick up. Instead of building a task board, the agent found one a colleague had built and added it to the project.
how_it_went: The poster says the tool was running in under five minutes. The developer kept expanding it over the next hour, and the board's code never needed to change.
worth_knowing: This depends on having a library of reusable parts your agent can find. The post comes from the company that makes the development environment used.
prompt: Before building anything new for [project name], search [our shared code library or repo] for existing parts that already do what I need, such as [task board, login screen, table]. List what you find and how each would fit. Wait for my choice, then add the chosen part to the project and connect it so that [describe the behavior, e.g. comments on code lines become tickets]. Do not change the shared part's own code.

curation.rationale: A real case of an agent finding and reusing a teammate's task board inside a new code review tool, but it is short, light on detail and partly promotes the company's product.
